rv.q: The piece is not, of course, the only work to look at the mostly triumphalist, patriarchal myths of the classical era from modern perspectives. "Hadestown," a hit Broadway musical, is another example, as is " An Iliad," the magnificent solo piece from Lisa Peterson and Denis O'Hare that looked at Homer through an anti-war lens.
Goodman Theatre's staging of Atwood's stage adaptation of 'The Penelopiad' shapes a production of furious impact and impeccable ensemble work from the all-female, 13-strong cast.
Even when I found the play's action to be slowly paced and lacking in dynamics, I was consistently captivated by the ensemble's performances.

This is a triumphant Goodman directing debut for Booth, establishing her as a potent creative voice in Chicago and perhaps acting as something of a cri de coeur presaging similarly powerful productions to come.
This is a tragedy full of all sorts of joys, from laughs to retribution. Don't miss it.

In Greek mythology, Penelope was the Queen, the devoted spouse and the good wife of King Odysseus. When her valiant husband is called to fight in the Trojan War, the loving and devoted Penelope struggles against all odds, including hundreds of persistent suitors, to remain faithful to her husband for the next 20 years.
"The Penelopiad" is a zesty romp and very entertaining.
Overall, I enjoyed The Penelopiad, but it needed some trimming of scenes, providing more focus on the exceptional scenes between Penelope and her deceptive nature that cost the maids their lives.
"The Penelopiad" is theater as it should be experienced: with the class, beauty and quality we expect from one of the city's greatest theatrical jewels: the Goodman Theatre.

The Penelopiad is a revelation. It’s no wonder the words of Margaret Atwood combined with the direction of Susan V. Booth , the acting of an all-star cast, and the remarkable design work of a talented team have combined to create a play that, like the poem it draws from, can only be described as epic.
